children: Shares of Bajaj Auto and Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) rose more than 1 percent each in morning trade on September 1 after the automakers reported strong sales growth for August, with exports recording particularly sharp gains.

Bajaj Auto shares rose 1.48 percent to Rs 12,310, while M&M gained 1.3 percent to Rs 3,324.80. Both stocks were among the top gainers on the Nifty 50, outperforming the broader market. At 9:37 am, the Nifty was down 33.70 points, or 0.14 percent, at 24,046.70, while the Sensex slipped 67.57 points, or 0.09 percent, to 76,889.70.
Bajaj Auto reported total sales of 5.35 lakh units in August, up 28 percent from 4.17 lakh units in the year-ago period. The figure was also comfortably ahead of Nomura's estimate of 4.88 lakh units.
The two-wheeler maker's exports surged 51 percent year-on-year to 2.80 lakh units from 1.85 lakh units, while domestic sales increased 10 percent to 2.55 lakh units from 2.33 lakh units.
Total two-wheeler sales climbed 30 percent year-on-year to 4.43 lakh units from 3.41 lakh units. Commercial vehicle sales rose 22 percent to 92,016 units, compared with 75,729 units a year earlier.
M&M, meanwhile, reported total sales of 1.07 lakh units for August, up 42 percent year-on-year and broadly in line with Nomura's estimate of 1.07 lakh units.
Passenger vehicle sales jumped 50 percent to 59,257 units from 39,399 units in the corresponding month last year. Exports were even stronger, surging 71 percent to 6,054 units from 3,548 units.
The company's tractor business recorded more modest growth. Total tractor sales increased 5 percent year-on-year to 29,507 units from 28,117 units, slightly below Nomura's estimate of 29,800 units.
